Note::slabs¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

std::vector<Note> Note::slabs() const

Decompose A Rank-Three Note Without Leaving Note Storage¶

slabs() separates an exactly rank-three Note along its leading axis. For a receiver with shape [planes, rows, columns], it returns planes Notes, each with shape [rows, columns]. The axis names are illustrative rather than prescriptive: a slab may represent a page, batch member, document grid, or any other two-dimensional slice selected by axis zero.

This method is structural extraction, not conversion to an external tensor type. Every result remains a Note, retains the receiver’s dtype, and supports the normal Note operations for that dtype. Use it when a rank-three value must be handed to code that processes one matrix-shaped Note at a time while still preserving the closed Note contract.

No cell payload is copied. Each returned Note is a contiguous view into the same intrusive backing allocation, beginning at source offset i * rows * columns. Creating the result therefore costs O(planes) small view objects rather than O(numel) cell copies. Those views participate in ownership: a retained slab keeps the shared allocation alive after the source handle is destroyed.

The receiver must be defined and have exactly three axes. Cardinality does not substitute for rank: a one-cell scalar, vector, or matrix is rejected, as is an undefined handle. Add or remove axes explicitly with unsqueeze(), squeeze(), or reshape() when such a structural change is part of the intended model.

Zero extents are preserved rather than collapsed. Shape [2, 0, 3] produces two empty Notes of shape [0, 3]; shape [0, 4, 5] produces no slabs at all. This distinction lets callers retain known inner geometry even when no cells are present.

Example 1: Address Slabs, Rows, And Columns¶

const auto cube = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{
        "000", "001", "010", "011", "100", "101", "110", "111"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 3>{2, 2, 2});
const auto cells = cube.slabs();

std::cout << "slab-shape=[" << cells[1].size(0) << ", "
          << cells[1].size(1) << "]"
          << " [1][0][1]=" << cells[1].at(1)
          << " [1][1][0]=" << cells[1].at(2) << '\n';

Output¶

slab-shape=[2, 2] [1][0][1]=101 [1][1][0]=110

at() is flat within each returned slab, so positions 1 and 2 correspond to coordinates [0, 1] and [1, 0] respectively.

Example 2: Preserve Empty Inner Geometry¶

const auto cells = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 3>{2, 0, 3}).slabs();

std::cout << "empty slabs=" << cells.size()
          << " shapes=[" << cells[0].size(0) << ", " << cells[0].size(1)
          << "],[" << cells[1].size(0) << ", " << cells[1].size(1) << "]\n";

Output¶

empty slabs=2 shapes=[0, 3],[0, 3]

Example 3: Preserve Native Dtype And Shared Lifetime¶

std::vector<pluss::Note> cells;
{
  const auto cube = pluss::note::make(
      std::vector<std::int64_t>{10, 11, 12, 13, 20, 21, 22, 23},
      std::array<std::int64_t, 3>{2, 2, 2});
  cells = cube.slabs();
}

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "int64=" << cells[1].is_int64()
          << " values=" << cells[1].integers()[0] << ','
          << cells[1].integers()[3] << '\n';

Output¶

int64=true values=20,23

The source handle has left scope, but cells[1] still owns a share of the integer allocation. This is stronger than a borrowed std::span, whose lifetime must remain nested inside that of its Note.

Example 4: An Empty Leading Axis Produces No Views¶

const auto cells = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 3>{0, 4, 5}).slabs();

std::cout << "slabs=" << cells.size() << '\n';

Output¶

slabs=0

Example 5: Lower Ranks Do Not Auto-Promote¶

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make({"x"}).slabs();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "slabs rank1: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

slabs rank1: rejected

Example 6: Undefined Is Not An Empty Rank-Three Note¶

try {
  (void)pluss::Note::undefined().slabs();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "slabs undefined: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

slabs undefined: rejected
